headline: IT'S CALLED A CYCLOID
AND IT HIDES A SECOND TRICK

package.title: Which Ramp Is Fastest?
alt_titles: The Shortest Path Is NOT The Fastest
The Curve That Breaks Your Intuition
description: Four ramps, same start, same finish, no friction. The straight line is the shortest path, but it isn't the fastest.

The winner is a cycloid: the curve traced by a point on a rolling wheel. It's the brachistochrone, the fastest possible slide under gravity (Johann Bernoulli's 1696 challenge, solved by Newton, Leibniz and the Bernoullis).

Its second trick: release balls from ANY height on a cycloid and they all reach the bottom at exactly the same moment. That makes it the tautochrone too (Huygens, 1659), with time to the bottom T = π√(r/g) whatever the start.
Every ball here moves by exact frictionless physics; every click is a fixed distance travelled.
